content: A socket bound to ::1 serves IPv6 loopback only; 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are distinct addresses and IPV6_V6ONLY=0 does not make a ::1-bound socket accept IPv4 - only binding the wildcard :: does, which also exposes every interface. Practical effect: binding ::1 is a genuinely narrow exposure but clients that resolve localhost to IPv4 first will get connection refused. Windows loopback traffic does not traverse the Windows Firewall, so no prompt appears and no rule is needed; the firewall GUI even rejects ::1 in rule scopes.
